newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss federal revenue on track for 97 budget-finmi.
newsitem.headline: Swiss federal revenue on track for 97 budget-finmi.

text.p: The Swiss federal finance ministry said that its fiscal revenues were on track to reach the budgeted level of 35 billion Swiss francs for the year, based on calculations for the first half of 1997.
At the same time, however, the government said it was uncertain whether expectations for a budget deficit this year of nearly six billion francs were on target.
In December, Switzerland's parliament approved a federal budget for 1997 with a deficit of 5.77 billion Swiss francs.

In its latest assessment, the finance ministry said federal spending was lower than expected in some cases, in part due to lower costs tied to interest payments, highway maintenance and cantonal claims to interest withholding tax.

The Federal government's expenditures for old-age pensions, higher education, export insurance and agriculture were also seen lower than expected. But federal unemployment insurance is expected to require additional loans of some hundreds of millions of Swiss francs from the government.

The finance ministry said that income from value-added tax and stamp tax were higher than expected. Stamp tax levied on bourse transactions was higher than projected due to high turnover on exchanges. Tobacco taxes, increased in March, were also above projection.
Interest withholding tax was lower, the finance ministry said, citing declines in interest rates.
